Preservation conditions will depend on the organism and can vary substantially, however such conditions should be chosen with the purpose of (i) limit DNA degradation during storage and (ii) ensure that key taxonomic features are retained for subsequent identification. However, in the context of marine non-indigenous species, many taxa (including most invertebrates) can be preserved frozen (-20°C to -80°C), using 70-100% Ethanol Absolute Lennox Catalog #CRTSE0021612 (RRID: ) (for subsequent DNA analysis, but may lead to discoloration affecting taxonomic ID) and/or Formalin solution neutral buffered 10% Merck MilliporeSigma (Sigma-Aldrich) Catalog #HT501128-4L (for subsequent taxonomic identification, but not recommended or DNA isolation). WARNING: caution should be exercised when handling ethanol and formalin. Please consult the relevant Safety Data Sheets for further information. steps.title: Collect specimens and record metadata
steps.instruction: Gather specimens using targeted surveys or opportunistic methods (hand collection, dredges, corers, traps, nets, or dedicated in‑situ approaches such as SETL settlement plates). Preserve whole specimens when possible. For each specimen, record minimum metadata: exact geographic coordinates, date of collection, collection method, photographs, and collector name/contact. Follow the detailed metadata guidelines of Rimet et al. (2021). Assign a unique specimen identifier code according to the intended database/repository format.

steps.title: Sort specimens into single‑species groups
steps.instruction: For bulk samples (e.g., dredge or SETL collections), separate organisms into groups representing single species. For organisms larger than 1 mm, rinse the substrate or specimen through a 1 mm sieve using clear seawater or artificial seawater. Examine the flow‑through water under a microscope to detect micro‑organisms.

steps.title: Disinfect waste materials
steps.instruction: Treat all used materials and liquids with an appropriate disinfectant (e.g., Virkon Aquatic, AgriDirect) before disposal to prevent spread of non‑indigenous species or pathogens.

steps.title: Select genetic marker and primers
steps.instruction: Choose a genetic marker based on the target organism and desired taxonomic resolution. Use the following validated assays and primer sets:

substeps.instruction: Assay 1 – Marine metazoans – COI – 658 bp – Forward: LoboF1 (KBTCHACAAAYCAYAARGAYATHGG, Lobo et al. 2013); Reverse: LoboR1 (TAAACYTCWGGRTGWCCRAARAAYCA, Lobo et al. 2013)
Assay 2 – Marine metazoans – COI – 313 bp – Forward: mICOIintF‑XT (GGWACWRGWTGRACWNTNTAYCCYCCY, Leray et al. 2013); Reverse: jgHCO2198a (TANACYTCNGGRTGNCCRAARAAYCA, Leray et al. 2013)
Assay 3 – Marine metazoans – COI – 710 bp – Forward: jgLCO1490 (TITCIACIAAYCAYAARGAYATTGG, Geller et al. 2013); Reverse: jgHCO2198b (TAIACYTCIGGRTGICCRAARAAYCA, Geller et al. 2013)
Assay 4 – Marine metazoans – 16S rRNA – 567 bp – Forward: 16sar‑L (CGCCTGTTTATCAAAAACAT, Palumbi et al. 2002); Reverse: 16sbr‑H (CCGGTCTGAACTCAGATCACGT, Palumbi et al. 2002)
Assay 5 – Freshwater diatoms – RuBisCO – 312 bp – Forward: Diat_rbcL_708F (AGGTGAARYWAAAGGTTCWTAYTTAAA, Vasselon et al. 2017); Reverse: Diat_rbcL_R3 (CCTTCTAATTTACCWACWACTG, Vasselon et al. 2017)

steps.title: Amplify DNA by PCR
steps.instruction: Perform PCR using the selected primer pair for the chosen assay, following standard PCR conditions appropriate for the primer set and target fragment.

steps.title: Verify PCR product by gel electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Run the PCR products on an agarose gel electrophoresis to confirm the expected amplicon size.

steps.title: Optional PCR clean‑up
steps.instruction: (Optional) If desired, clean the PCR product using a suitable PCR clean‑up method before sequencing; many cases do not require this step.

steps.title: Submit PCR product for Sanger sequencing
steps.instruction: Send the verified PCR product for Sanger sequencing using the forward and/or reverse primers employed in the amplification.

steps.title: Inspect and curate raw sequence data
steps.instruction: Examine the raw DNA sequence data with appropriate software (e.g., MEGA, Geneious). Curate the sequences to ensure they are high‑quality and error‑free.

steps.title: Deposit sequences in public repositories
steps.instruction: Upload the curated DNA sequences to public databases such as GenBank and BOLD, linking each sequence to its specimen identifier and metadata.
